chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Hammad, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The false oath (al-yamin al-ghamoos) — calamities are awaited with it for forty nights.

key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً: Forty nights — a significant period indicating the swiftness of divine retribution
key_terms.الْيَمِينُ الْغَمُوسُ: Al-yamin al-ghamoos: the false/perjurous oath; literally 'the immersing oath' — so called because it plunges its swearer into sin and hellfire
key_terms.يُنْتَظَرُ: Is awaited/expected — indicating a certain and forthcoming divine punishment

ai.seo_question: What is al-yamin al-ghamoos (false oath) and what are its consequences in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a grave warning about the al-yamin al-ghamoos — the 'immersing false oath,' so named because it submerges its swearer in sin and hellfire. The Imam states that one who swears such a false oath will experience calamities and misfortune within forty nights, indicating a rapid divine recompense in this world. This teaching was directed at early Muslim communities where oaths were used in legal disputes and commerce, and where swearing falsely was a serious moral and legal transgression.
